question: What structural conditions on a compositional data-generating process, the training support, and a model are sufficient to guarantee generalization to unseen combinations of familiar components?

key_findings.claim: Compositionality is formalized as a property of a generator, not merely a dataset: independent component functions map factorized latents to hidden components that a shared composition function combines.
key_findings.evidence: Definition 1 writes f(z)=C(phi_1(z_1),...,phi_K(z_K)). Definition 2 then separates compositional generalization from ordinary interpolation or extrapolation by requiring training and test distributions to have equal support for every marginal component, even when their joint supports differ.

key_findings.claim: Matching every component marginal is not enough when the composition hides information; training support must also permit reconstruction of each component's local effect.
key_findings.evidence: Definition 3 requires, for every component value, a finite set of same-component training points whose composition-function derivative blocks collectively have full rank. In the sprite example, a narrow diagonal support always occludes part of a background sprite, whereas sufficient foreground variation reveals every pixel and recovers the relevant Jacobian.

key_findings.claim: Under differentiability, compositional and sufficient support, a shared known composition function and latent factorization, and one aligned initial point, perfect training-support fit guarantees fit on the compositional test support.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 1 first reconstructs component-function Jacobians despite a potentially noninvertible composition, integrates them using the initial-point equality, and then recombines component values available through marginal support. This is a noiseless sufficient theorem: it does not bound test error from nonzero empirical training error.

key_findings.claim: Controlled multi-sprite experiments support the theorem's qualitative distinctions, while also demonstrating that its conditions are not necessary.
key_findings.evidence: A monolithic network fits orthogonal-support training data but obtains negative all-space R-squared, whereas the matched compositional model reaches about 0.951. Removing marginal coverage or making diagonal support too narrow degrades unseen-combination reconstruction in the predicted regions. Yet an RGB-alpha model whose composition Jacobian cannot satisfy the stated full-rank condition generalizes best, proving the sufficient condition can be loose.

method.core_idea: Factor the ground-truth and learned maps into independent component functions plus a composition function, then use support coverage and Jacobian rank to characterize when agreement on training combinations forces agreement on new combinations.
method.mechanism: The proof uses equal marginal support to source every test component from training, a full-rank sum of composition derivatives to identify each hidden component Jacobian, and an initial point to remove integration constants. Experiments train component-wise and monolithic image decoders on 100k two-sprite samples for 2,000 epochs, then measure reconstruction over in-domain and full-product latent supports under targeted support and composition ablations.
assumptions: Ground-truth component latents and their correct factorization are observed during supervised training.
The learned and true generators share a known composition function and latent factorization.
Component maps are differentiable, the composition is Lipschitz, and the relevant training support lies in an open set.
The learned model matches the true generator exactly throughout the training support rather than only at finitely sampled points.
A component-space initial point is aligned between the true and learned decompositions.
The existence of one qualifying compositional representation is sufficient even though representations are non-unique.

techniques.role: Defines component functions and their composition independently of a particular observed dataset.
Distinguishes unseen combinations from unseen component values.
Tests whether varied contexts expose every dimension of a hidden component.
Identifies local component maps from observable generator derivatives.
Varies orthogonal, diagonal, broad, narrow, and gapped training supports.
Separates compositional architectural bias from parameter capacity.

evaluations.setting: Two-sprite supervised reconstruction with random full-product training data
evaluations.metric: MSE and variance-weighted R-squared over in-domain and all latent combinations
evaluations.result: Both monolithic and compositional decoders fit the fully covered task, with the compositional model achieving lower error.

evaluations.setting: Orthogonal and diagonal supports satisfying both theorem support conditions
evaluations.result: The compositional decoder generalizes to unseen combinations while the monolithic model fails sharply on orthogonal support; several valid support geometries work similarly.

evaluations.setting: Gapped marginal support and narrow diagonal support
evaluations.metric: Spatial error heatmaps, all-space MSE, and R-squared
evaluations.result: Errors concentrate where component values are absent, and persistent occlusion from insufficient context variation substantially degrades generalization.
evaluations.baseline: Broad supports satisfying compositional and sufficient support

evaluations.setting: RGB-alpha component representation with alpha composition
evaluations.result: The model generalizes despite a composition derivative that cannot meet the theorem's full-rank condition, illustrating non-necessity.
evaluations.baseline: RGB component outputs with soft pixel-wise composition

limitations: The guarantee is supervised and assumes access to ground-truth component latents; the intended unsupervised representation-learning problem remains open.
The correct latent factorization and composition function are assumed known and shared by the learned model, which is implausible in domains such as language.
Exact functional agreement over a continuous training support is much stronger than finite noisy empirical risk minimization, and no finite-sample or approximation-error bound is supplied.
The aligned initial component point is required by the proof even though experiments do not enforce it.
The sufficient-support rank condition is not necessary, as the paper's own alpha-compositing experiment demonstrates.
Validation uses one synthetic two-sprite reconstruction family with fixed rendering and 10k test samples, not natural scenes, language, reasoning, or downstream decisions.
Training-distribution density, stochasticity, optimization, sample complexity, and learned shortcuts are largely abstracted away in favor of support-level statements.
A compositional function representation always has trivial forms, so the scientific content depends on choosing a meaningful factorization and simple composition.
failure_modes: All component marginals are covered, but co-occurrence patterns keep one component dimension permanently occluded.
A model uses an entangled decomposition that fits training data but does not share the assumed composition map.
Finite samples leave holes inside a theoretically open support, making derivative reconstruction statistically ill-conditioned.
Small train error accumulates through Jacobian integration and becomes large for distant combinations.
The composition rule changes between train and test even though individual components are familiar.
A nominally compositional architecture memorizes joint configurations rather than learning independent component functions.
A support passes the binary rank test but has a poor condition number and therefore requires impractical sample precision.
reusable_insights: Design compositional splits by checking marginal component coverage separately from joint-combination novelty.
Vary each component across contexts that reveal its full effect; marginal coverage alone can be observationally insufficient.
Use support-violation heatmaps and matched monolithic controls to test whether an architecture truly recombines components.
Distinguish sufficient theoretical conditions from necessary empirical design rules.
Replace binary Jacobian rank with singular-value or condition-number diagnostics when turning the theorem into a dataset audit.
Evaluate finite-sample error transfer rather than extrapolating exact-fit theorems to trained systems.
open_questions: Can the guarantee be extended to approximate fit with finite-sample, noise, and conditioning-dependent error bounds?
Can component identities and the composition function be learned unsupervised under testable assumptions?
What weaker condition replaces the aligned initial point and the sufficient-support full-rank requirement?
How can support adequacy be estimated from observations when ground-truth latents and generator derivatives are unavailable?
Which inductive biases legitimately bridge gaps in support without encouraging shortcut extrapolation?
Do the support conditions predict performance on natural multi-object, language, music, and embodied reasoning tasks?
How should causal interactions and hierarchical components be represented when components are not independent peers?

competitive_landscape.title: Measuring Compositional Generalization: A Comprehensive Method on Realistic Data
competitive_landscape.difference: Keysers et al. construct realistic language splits with high compound divergence while controlling atom divergence and empirically expose model failures. The reviewed work supplies a generator/support theorem, but validates only synthetic vision and does not operationalize realistic benchmark construction.

competitive_landscape.title: Provable Compositional Generalization for Object-Centric Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: Wiedemer et al. extend the program to object-centric autoencoders, proving conditions for learned slots to generalize without supplied component latents and validating common object-centric models. It addresses the reviewed theorem's largest stated gap while remaining focused on object scenes.

competitive_landscape.title: When does compositional structure yield compositional generalization? A kernel theory
competitive_landscape.difference: Lippl and Stachenfeld analyze fixed-representation kernel learners and reveal conjunction-wise additivity, memorization leak, shortcut bias, and tasks that cannot compositionally generalize. Their theory covers density and task interactions that a support-only exact-fit guarantee omits, while assuming the kernel regime rather than an identifiable generator.

competitive_landscape.title: Interaction Asymmetry: A General Principle for Learning Composable Abstractions
competitive_landscape.difference: Brady et al. use higher-order block-diagonal derivative structure to recover composable concepts without supervision and propose a Transformer-VAE regularizer. It relaxes explicit component supervision and broadens allowable generator interactions, at the cost of new derivative-structure and capacity assumptions.

competitive_landscape.title: Successes and Limitations of Object-centric Models at Compositional Generalisation
competitive_landscape.difference: Montero et al. test whether object-centric benefits extend from novel scene compositions to novel object-property compositions and identify both training-dependent gains and a remaining limitation. This provides empirical scope checks beyond the reviewed paper's supervised renderer.

novelty_assessment: The paper's valuable shift is to define compositionality at the generator level and separate marginal support from context-dependent observability through a Jacobian-rank condition. This yields a clean sufficient theorem and falsifiable support ablations, but the exact-fit, known-composition, supervised assumptions leave much of modern compositional learning outside its guarantee. Later object-centric and kernel theories directly address those omissions, so the work is best viewed as a foundational formal vocabulary and proof template rather than a practical generalization solution.
reviewer_notes: Read all 16 extracted pages, including the complete theorem proof, composition examples, experimental protocol, support violations, and discussion. Preserved the distinction between compositional marginal support and sufficient observational support, and explicitly reported the paper's counterexample to necessity. Five primary arXiv/OpenReview works were checked on 2026-08-23.
